title: The Lord's Popularity
text: “Hmm… what is this, I wonder… is it like one of those challenge-mode games where a salaryman from the distant past receives a treasure map from an old man after some incident, proceeds without killing the old man to steal it, only to have the old man steal it back and kill him at the very end?”

So analyzed Father in my head. “Why do I even have this knowledge?” I wondered… but I vaguely recalled a retro game-obsessed pig rambling about some garbage game like that, so it might have gotten mixed in there. Now that I think about it, I believe Father also talked about a game like that once, back when the world had become peaceful and I took him to a dungeon in this world.

I think it’s probably that latter memory, actually. Father has told me about all sorts of games over the years, I say. That wealth of information is quite the rare treasure, indeed. Incidentally, in that game, apparently you have to cut ties with your wife—since she’s a pig—and quit your company too, and if you let the pig and the company president get too cozy before calling your wife back, it kills the mood and, more importantly, creates a whole bunch of extra hassle. One mustn’t mishandle the situation, it seems.

Taking that as a reference, I too have been doing various things this time around to avoid mishandling matters. If I don’t dispose of the Crimson Swine, the hassle only multiplies. Based on various testimonies, I recalled an incident where I actually recreated that very game in this world. Usually it’s made by members of the Filolial-sama Fan Club, including Filo-tan, all gathering together to build it.
It’s a game where you splice together Filo-tan’s voice clips to simulate school life, I say!

Using devices like the terminals that exist in this world, combined with alchemy, I created such a thing. When I showed it to Father… he said, “Oh, I never imagined you could make a dating sim in another world.” And then he added, “A dating sim Motoyasu made… hearing that makes me a little worried about what it implies, but wow, the reproduction quality is pretty high.” It’s a complete school-life simulation starring Filo-tan, I say. Incidentally, when I showed this game to Filo-tan herself, she apparently mistook the device for a toy meant to be kicked, and kicked it to pieces.
“Boo! Filo never says stuff like that! You spliced it together to make me say weird things! Master!”

Hahaha! Such a fun recreation of school life with Filo-tan, indeed. I thought I heard a voice—whose, I couldn’t tell—muttering “What on earth is this guy thinking…” but surely that was just my imagination. Banishing Rival to another world is simple, I say. It costs a fair bit, but you just hold onto a dragon egg for a while and then toss it into another world. Of course, I’ve secured a portal, so I can still go there! Simple, indeed. The hard part comes after—swiftly closing off every single wave-connection to that other world so Rival can’t come back here. That’s the method it used last loop, I say. I’m not sure which specific wave it was, but well, I doubt Rival will show up during the very first wave of the world. Why? Because I’ll be banishing the egg several hours before the wave even strikes. Even Rival, freshly hatched, surely can’t rush to the wave site that fast! Now then, to summarize further, the goal should be to minimize wave damage as much as possible.
■ How to minimize damage from the first wave? · Prevent Big Sister’s village fishermen from setting sail · Ensure Éclair’s parents survive

Even if I reduce the wave damage to the village, it won’t do much good if the population is depleted anyway—plus, minimizing wave casualties is the whole point here. Well, as I’d considered before, let’s handle this by sinking the ship.
“Now then, time to purchase a Filolial-sama egg, I say!”

I headed straight to the Filolial breeder’s place. There, I tried to secure the eggs belonging to Yuki-chan and the others… but the eggs that should have been there weren’t. They hadn’t been placed in storage yet, it seemed. After looping so many times, I’ve come to recognize by scent which eggs will become Yuki-chan and the others, but there was nothing there. Hmm… it seems I’m a bit too early. So, without making a purchase, I left word with the breeder to simply continue as usual, and that I’d return again when the time came. Even Yuki-chan’s egg hadn’t been placed yet. Well, since Yuki-chan’s parents are apparently racehorses, I could probably identify and secure them specifically if I wanted to. Ah, but poking around carelessly might stir up all sorts of dangerous changes. Best to keep contact to an absolute minimum. Ahh… if I push forward with securing Filolial-sama in this state, the resulting changes could spiral out considerably. There’s a chance I might never meet Father and Filo-tan again because of it, so I’d rather not alter things too much here. And so, securing Filolial-sama will have to be postponed, I say… gnnh, how frustrating.
“Haah…”

And so, three days remain until the wave. It’s a shock that I haven’t managed to secure Yuki-chan and the others, but there are things that must be done regardless. In between tasks, I rushed to Wolf’s family home to check on the scene of Takt’s crime, only to find the trees already cleared away—so preventing that is probably no longer possible. Still, well… with so much to confirm, securing time to sleep has become quite the challenge, I say.
“Everyone, I beg of you.”
Éclair’s parents had arrived at the territory, and I was arranging for them to send men out to fish for the Crimson Swine.
“Lord, please don’t trouble yourself over it. Fishing is our trade, after all… though this particular catch will take a bit longer than usual, so please forgive the delay.”
“Indeed.”
“So there you have it, everyone! This is where we sea-faring men show our true mettle! Our hard work is what’ll raise the lord’s standing this time around! Let’s bring back the finest fish there is!”
“““Oooooh!”””

With that kind of energy, they set about loading all sorts of supplies onto the ship, clearly preparing for departure. From what I overheard eavesdropping, it sounded like they’d be setting off tomorrow. Rather quick departure, that—but well… I recall that when the wave struck while they were out on the open sea, the ocean grew violent, and everyone except Older Sister perished. It must have been quite the ordeal.
“Boo boo boo! Boo boo!”
“Hey now, Keel! Calm down.”
“Boo boo boo boo!”
“You’re still too young for this!”

…There was a fisherman there, stroking the head of what appeared to be the pig Keel, trying to soothe her. Judging by the shape of the ears, some kind of dog-type beastman. A gruff-looking man with a stern face.
“Boo-boo! Boo-heeh!”

Keel, for her part, was crying out energetically about something. A young girl who seemed to be Big Sister, along with what looked like fellow kin presumed to be her parents, watched the scene with gentle eyes.
“I’m grateful you arranged this for us.”
“Oh, not at all. If it’s a request from Lady Seaetto, every man in this village is eager to lend a hand. It’s no credit to us. It’s all thanks to Lady Seaetto’s good standing with the people.”
The man who appeared to be Big Sister’s father spoke with modest humility. Hmm… that warm, gentle air reminds me somewhat of Father.
“Tonight we drink hard and build up our vigor for tomorrow!”
The one who seemed to be Keel’s parent shouted this out with great excitement.
“Oooooh!”

The fishermen cheered in response, already preparing drinks to enjoy before their departure. Big Sister’s parent joined in helping with a cheerful expression as well. The way he moved so naturally with the mood, that cheerful face of his… hmm, reading the room while still enjoying himself—it resembles Father’s demeanor when he’s in one of his more easygoing, jovial moods. The expression, or rather the whole atmosphere, really does feel that way. Even from a distance, I can tell he’s quite well-regarded by the people here.

That said… it does make him a bit hard to approach. Big Sister and her kin have a keen ability to sense me even while I’m concealed. If I get too close to one of Big Sister’s relatives, there’s a real risk of being noticed. Just being able to listen in on their voices already feels like walking a dangerously thin line.

Still, well… this is what Big Sister and her village looked like before the wave struck. Father will go on to restore it afterward, but naturally, there are plenty of differences now. Remembering the ruins left after the wave stirs up in me a feeling of wanting to do something about it, no matter what. And yet, for that very reason, it pains me that I must sink this great ship they’re so desperately packing right now. Well, considering the sea will be too rough for work for a while afterward anyway, I suppose I’ll have to be forgiven for it. Worst case, I’ll just send the village some money anonymously.
